Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
403 AM PDT Fri Oct 16 2026

.SYNOPSIS...15/1247 PM.

A moderate to strong Santa Ana Wind will bring widespread strong
winds and critical fire weather conditions to much of Southwest 
California through Saturday. Additionally, very warm temperatures 
bring a high risk of heat illness to all coastal areas. A 
significant cool down is expected Sunday with a chance of 
widespread rain by Tuesday or Wednesday.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-SUN)...16/359 AM.

We are on track for the longest and strongest period of Santa Ana
winds today, especially at lower elevations (coastal valleys to
coast) with strongest cooridor of winds sliding a bit north into 
a more traditional Santa Ana setup.

High wind warnings and strong wind advisories look good for much
of Ventura and Los Angeles Counties with peak winds likely in the
50 to 70 mph range through late morning or early afternoon before
gradually weakening. Breezy east to northeast winds with gusts of
25 to 45 mph will also extend to most other areas that do not 
typically get much winds in this type of setup. Red Flag Warnings
also continue to be in effect for a large portion of Southwest 
California. Please take care with fire ignition sources.

Moderate-to-high heat risk is equally concerning, especially near
the coast with highs again in the 90s to near 100. Temperatures
will shoot up quickly this morning and stay quite warm well into
the evening, especially where breezy winds continue, increasing
the duration of the heat, which is particularly concerning for
those without air conditioning or that spend significant time 
outdoors. A Heat Advisory continues near the coast through
Saturday.

On Saturday, upper level support and surface gradients weaken but
still expecting a windy day, albeit probably 15-30 mph weaker than
Friday. And with the offshore flow and cold advection weakening as
well temperatures at the coast should cool at least a few degrees
while valleys and other interior areas either remain the same or 
warm slightly. 

A digging trough from the northwest and the return of onshore 
flow will bring significant cooling and moistening trends along 
with breezy northwest to onshore winds to the region. Daytime
highs by Monday will mostly be in the 70s with a sprinkling of low
80s for warmer valleys. Signs of potentially inclement weather 
are likely by Monday night in the form of increasing mid to high 
clouds.

.LONG TERM (MON-THU)...16/359 AM.

There is increasing confidence in rain chances next week, though 
low confidence on the details. Virtually all the solutions 
indicate at least some light rain, most likely starting Wednesday,
but could start as early as Tuesday afternoon or as late as 
Wednesday evening. Rain amounts are even more scattered but mostly
around a half inch area-wide. We may not have a good handle on 
this system until early next week as our guidance struggles with 
storms coming from the northwest, especially closed, cut-off low 
pressure systems. There are more than a few solutions that bring 
an inch or more so there a small potential for heavy rain/flood 
concerns.

&&

.AVIATION...16/0822Z.

At 06Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer or inversion. 

High confidence in CAVU conditions for all sites through the 
period. Moderate confidence in direction/strength of northeast- 
east winds, gusts may be off by 020-030 degrees and 10-15 knots 
respectively.

KLAX...High confidence in 06Z in CAVU conditions through the 
period. Moderate confidence in winds, and there is the potential 
for an extended period of gusty easterly winds from about 17Z to 
22Z, with gusts up to 25 kt. 

KBUR...High confidence in CAVU conditions through the TAF period.
Moderate confidence in winds as timing may be off by 2-3 hours and
strength could be +/- 10 knots.

&&

.MARINE...16/122 AM.

For the Outer Waters, moderate to high confidence in current 
forecast. Through Sunday, high confidence in winds and seas 
remaining below Small Craft Advisory (SCA) levels across 
PZZ670/673. For PZZ676, there is a 60-80% chance of SCA level 
winds today. On Monday and Tuesday, there is a 50-60% chance of 
SCA level winds across all of the Outer Waters with seas hovering 
around SCA levels. 

For the Inner Waters north of Point Sal, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. There is a 40-50% chance of SCA 
level northeast winds this morning. For Saturday and Sunday, high
confidence in winds and seas remaining below SCA levels. On 
Monday and Tuesday, there is a 50% chance of SCA level winds, 
mainly in the afternoon and evening hours with seas hovering near 
SCA levels. 

For the Inner Waters south of Point Conception, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. There is a 60-70% chance of GALE 
force winds from Ventura to Santa Monica with a 40-60% chance of 
SCA level winds elsewhere (especially across the San Pedro 
Channel). For tonight and Saturday, there is a 50% chance of SCA 
level northeast winds from Point Mugu to Santa Monica with high 
confidence in winds and seas remaining below SCA levels elsewhere.
For Sunday through Tuesday, high confidence in winds and seas 
remaining below SCA levels for most areas except for the western 
half of the Santa Barbara Channel where there is a 50-60% chance 
of SCA level winds.
